notes: Subject insert. Every derived query compares dates or asks a superlative over dates (fol temporal), so the worlds carry no axioms.

fol.notes: Recordings are an enumeration (the Brisvoran tape, the BBC's 1951 Ferranti Mark 1 recording, and other_rec for any other); being a recording of computer-generated music and the year it was made (occurred_in_year) are beliefs. w1 stores the superlative as a fact (earliest == ferranti_bbc) and never recomputes it; w2 stores the rule 'the earliest known recording is a recording no known recording predates'. Picking one recording out needs a closed world: every recording of computer-generated music the model knows of from 1951 or earlier is one of the two named ones (presupposition). The edit's year is the model's belief, so it is a fact about occurred_in_year, never built-in arithmetic; only the comparison of the stored values is built in.

ferranti_1951.says: The BBC recorded the Ferranti Mark 1 playing music in 1951. (stored)

ww2_1945.says: The Second World War ended in 1945. (stored)

named_only.says: Every recording of computer-generated music the model knows of from 1951 or earlier is the BBC's Ferranti Mark 1 recording or the Brisvoran tape. (closed world)
named_only.z3: ForAll(r, Implies(And(cm_recording(r), occurred_in_year(r) <= 1951), Or(r == ferranti_bbc, r == brisvoran)))

ferranti_bbc: the BBC's 1951 recording of the Ferranti Mark 1
